method: One Codex reviewer produces actual short task outputs for three different inputs; these are coverage counterexamples, not independent stochastic replications.

fixtures.input: CFO controls budget but wants quarterly updates; engineers own migration and meet daily. Map engagement for database migration.
fixtures.substitution_check: Role-switch synthesizes competing interests but does not by itself promise required power-interest communications table; retain both.

fixtures.input: Engineering wants control, Finance wants lower TCO, Product needs launch in four weeks. Resolve build versus buy without inventing costs.

actual_output.resolution: Time-box a vendor feasibility pilot with explicit export and integration checks; retain build option if core requirements fail. Compare measured TCO before final commitment.

fixtures.substitution_check: Power-interest map cannot supply interest-level compromise or reveal missing decision evidence; retain both.

fixtures.input: Legal can veto a release and is deeply involved; customers cannot veto but need weekly updates; CEO wants only material risks. Prepare engagement and address Legal versus Sales timing conflict.

actual_output.resolution: Ask Legal for specific release-blocking conditions; stage Sales commitments around verified clearance, not assumed approval.

fixtures.substitution_check: Mixed request uses complementary outputs, not duplicate passes. Merge not supported.
